statement: In zsh, an unquoted $VAR holding several words is one argument, so a list built in a variable reaches a command as a single path and the command can pass doing nothing. Incident: on 2026-11-03 the reviewing session, in the Bash tool's zsh, ran `set -- $p` to split 'PR head' pairs, and created two worktrees at main under paths containing a space instead of at the PR heads. Later, `npx vitest run $F`, with F listing 18 test files, printed no results, and the session nearly read a heading mutation as uncaught. Both were caught only by reading the output: `git worktree list` showed the paths, and the test summary line was absent. Fix: expand lists with ${=VAR} or an array in zsh, and confirm the effect (worktree HEAD, the test-file count) before reading a result. Rule: a command fed a list must report how many items it got.

movesWhen.reason: A review-method error by the reviewing session: no code change fixes it; the rule is to expand lists explicitly in zsh and confirm the item count a command received before reading its result.
